title: Loss from inferior coal tops Rs. 18.3 b | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:00
-     - 7

Inferior-quality coal has led to losses amounting to Rs. 18.3 billion, Parliament’s Sectoral Oversight Committee on Infrastructure and Strategic Development Chairman, SJB MP S.M. Marikkar said yesterday, tabling an expert committee report on the losses.

The report, dated 7 October, 2026, puts the additional cost and financial loss from the use of substandard coal at Rs. 15.7 billion between 1 January and 15 September. It separately calculates a Rs. 2.3 billion premium paid on emergency coal procurement, which the committee said should not be considered a financial loss in isolation.

The committee was appointed by the Sectoral Oversight Committee on 5 August and chaired by Ministry of Energy Additional Secretary K.L.R.C. Wijayasinghe, with officials from the Ministry, the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL), National System Operator (Pvt.) Ltd. (NSO), the Lakvijaya Power Plant and Lanka Coal Company (Pvt.) Ltd. Electricity Generation Lanka (Pvt.) Ltd. (EGL) Chairman Prof. Saliya Jayasekara withdrew from the committee at his own request, citing a potential conflict of interest.

The coal in question was supplied by India’s Trident Chemphar Ltd. under a term tender to deliver 1.5 million MT to the Lakvijaya plant in Norochcholai between December 2025 and May 2026. Although 25 shipments were planned, only 19 were received due to issues of quality, the report said. The first arrived on 31 December, 2025 and the last on 3 July, 2026.

The largest component, Rs. 7.1 billion, stems from higher coal consumption. The plant burnt 0.4419 kg of Trident coal per kWh against a standard rate of 0.3742 kg/kWh drawn from 2018 to 2025 data, about 18% more coal for each unit of electricity. The committee estimated the shortfall at 461,838 MWh of energy, requiring an additional 172,820 MT of coal valued at Rs. 41.08 per kg. It assumed no factor other than the low quality of coal contributed to the higher consumption.

A further Rs. 8.6 billion was spent buying electricity from other sources to offset the plant’s reduced output between 21 January and 15 September. The plant’s generation fell by 197,673 MWh over the period, of which 35,210 MWh was covered by hydropower and the rest largely by diesel plants. This includes Rs. 402.8 million to replace 15,225 MWh lost due to the delayed arrival of the last emergency shipment.

Additional maintenance accounted for Rs. 80.4 million, an estimate covering only Unit 1, which was under maintenance at the time. Inspections in August found severe ash fouling and heavily solidified ash in the boiler’s air preheaters, which warm incoming combustion air using exhaust heat, requiring Rs. 67.5 million to dismantle, clean and reinstall the heating elements. Cleaning accumulated ash in the boiler is to cost Rs. 11.6 million and coal mill repairs Rs. 1.3 million. Costs for the remaining two units cannot be estimated until internal inspections are conducted, the report said. Extra ash and pyrite handling cost another Rs. 13.1 million.

The emergency procurement, carried out under a Cabinet decision of 26 January in case Trident failed to meet its obligations, brought in five shipments from Taranjot Resources (Pvt.) Ltd. at a fixed $ 142 per MT. Had they been bought under the term tender pricing formula, the price would have been $ 116.68 to $ 123.95 per MT, putting the additional cost at $ 7.2 million. The committee said the emergency procurement was a prudent risk mitigation measure, as sourcing the five shipments from Trident would have depleted stocks faster and risked shortages and power cuts.

The report also excludes the cost of burning coal equivalent to 270 MW to generate 220 MW due to its low calorific value. PUCSL, in a note annexed to the report, said the assessment underestimates the actual economic impact. It argued the hydropower used to fill the shortfall should be valued at the system marginal cost rather than zero, as reservoir levels were not at spilling conditions and were reported to be relatively low at times. It also said diesel generation had been costed at subsidised prices that do not reflect the actual economic cost borne by the country.

EGL, in a submission annexed to the report, also noted a 14,698 MT gap between the 1.997 million MT recorded in load port reports and the 1.982 million MT consumed, attributing it to coal left uncollected in the plant’s 42-acre coal yard.

The figure is the highest in a series of loss estimates SJB MP Marikkar has presented on the coal since early this year. In March, citing PUCSL, he told Parliament the first nine shipments had caused a loss of Rs. 8.5 billion. By May, he claimed all 17 shipments received to that point were substandard and that losses could exceed Rs. 30 billion.

title: Govt. denies substandard coal  behind Lakvijaya failure | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:30
-     - 8

Cabinet Spokesperson and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa yesterday rejected Opposition allegations that substandard coal contributed to the failure of Generator Unit 1 at the Lakvijaya Power Plant in Norochcholai during the nationwide blackout on Saturday. 

Coal from a new shipment had been used for power generation since 4 September, he told journalists.

“There is no link between the coal quality and this incident, as the coal used since 4 September is from new shipments,” Dr. Jayatissa said.

The generator had been shut down for maintenance for 62 days from 30 July to 30 September, he said. Unit 1 remains offline following the technical failure, and Dr. Jayatissa expressed hope that the plant would return to normal operations from tomorrow, in line with assurances given by the authorities.

Asked about the financial losses caused by the outage, which journalists said the opposition was calculating, Dr. Jayatissa said the opposition would announce those figures next week. “Our job is to restore the system,” he said.

title: 92% of taxpayers yet to file returns ahead of Nov. deadline | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:28
-     - 12

Around 91.7% of Sri Lanka’s registered individual taxpayers are yet to file income tax returns for the 2025/2026 year of assessment ahead of the November deadline, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) said, warning of fines, additional assessments and prosecution for non-compliance.

Only about 100,000 returns have been filed since the online facility opened on 1 July, out of nearly 1.2 million registered taxpayers, leaving nearly 1.1 million outstanding, IRD Deputy Commissioner General J.M.S.S. Rathnawardene told a press conference on Monday (19). The low number may be due to a lack of awareness or the assumption that there is still plenty of time, he said, urging taxpayers not to wait until the last minute.

Everyone registered must file, including those with no taxable income and those whose tax has already been deducted from salaries or interest income, Rathnawardene said. Those who fail to do so may be fined up to Rs. 400,000, and the Commissioner General may issue an additional assessment or initiate legal proceedings. A person convicted by a Magistrate’s Court could be jailed for up to six months.

Returns must be filed online through the IRD’s Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS), IRD Commissioner General Nandana Kumara said. Taxpayers need a password or one-time password (OTP), which can be requested through ‘Access to e-Services’ on ird.gov.lk. If a taxpayer’s email address has not been updated, the password can be sent by post, or taxpayers can email ci@ird.gov.lk with a scanned National Identity Card and a written request to update it.

Those whose income is limited to salaries and interest can use a simplified return, which is mostly auto-filled, while those with business income must file the standard return. Kumara said taxpayers should ensure they receive the acknowledgement issued on successful submission, as it confirms the return was filed on time.

IRD officers at the head office and regional offices will assist taxpayers free of charge, IRD Deputy Commissioner General Dr. Nadee Dissanayake said. Guidance is available at the Advisory and Promotion Unit on the second floor of the head office, and through instructional videos on the IRD’s YouTube channel and Facebook page. Technical help is available through the call centre on 1944, though delays are possible due to limited staff.

title: Presidential probe into coal imports  extended to 16 Dec. | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:28
-     - 9

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake yesterday extended until 16 December, 2026 the term of the Special Presidential Commission of Inquiry investigating alleged irregularities in coal imports and related operations of Lanka Coal Ltd. 

The extension was announced through Extraordinary Gazette No. 2510/81, issued under Section 4 of the Special Presidential Commissions of Inquiry Act, No. 4 of 1978. The Commission’s previous term ended on 16 October, 2026, and the extension will allow it to continue its investigations, complete its inquiries and submit its final findings.

The Commission was established through Extraordinary Gazette No. 2484/08 on 17 April, 2026. Its mandate is to investigate alleged irregularities and illegal activities relating to coal imports, coal-based electricity generation and associated procurement operations of Lanka Coal (Private) Limited. The inquiry covers the period from the commencement of coal power generation up to 16 April, 2026.

The three-member Commission comprises Supreme Court Judge Kulugammana Mudiyanselage Gihan Himanu Kulugammana, Court of Appeal Judge Aditya Karunaratne Maddumapatabendige and High Court Judge Hettisinghege Sanjeewa Somaratne.

The extension comes days after an expert committee report tabled in Parliament put the cost of substandard coal supplied to the Lakvijaya Power Plant between January and September this year at Rs. 15.7 billion. That total comprises Rs. 7.1 billion in higher coal consumption and Rs. 8.6 billion spent on replacement power. The report separately calculated a Rs. 2.3 billion premium on emergency coal procurement.

title: Cabinet approves gazetting National Agency for PPPs Bill | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:26
-     - 9

Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa

The Cabinet of Ministers at their meeting on Monday approved the publication in the Government Gazette of a draft Bill to establish a National Agency for Public Private Partnerships (PPP) and to provide a legal framework for promoting and facilitating such projects in Sri Lanka. The Bill will then be submitted to Parliament for approval.

The Cabinet first approved the introduction of a new Act on 2 June 2025. The draft Bill has since been prepared by the Legal Draftsman and cleared by the Attorney General. 

Speaking at the weekly post-Cabinet media briefing, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said the legislation was shaped by opportunities and challenges identified in PPPs in recent years.

“Specifically, this includes establishing a comprehensive statutory and legal framework for identifying, formulating, evaluating, approving, procuring, implementing, monitoring, and concluding PPP projects,” he said.

The National Agency for PPP will facilitate, advise, coordinate, monitor and assist in executing PPP projects across all sectors of the economy.

The Bill also seeks to integrate PPP projects with the public investment management framework set up under the Public Financial Management Act, and to ensure fiscal discipline and consistency in project approval and monitoring.

It provides for a transparent, competitive procurement framework to select private partners in line with guidelines issued by the National Procurement Commission.

“This Bill is being drafted to place PPPs on a much more structured and formalised footing,” Dr. Jayatissa said.

Sri Lanka’s difficulty in executing PPPs for major infrastructure and national investment projects has stemmed from institutional, legal and political bottlenecks. Among them are policy unpredictability and abrupt changes of government, which have often led to the renegotiation, suspension or cancellation of major foreign-backed projects, eroding investor confidence.

He acknowledged that previous attempts to implement PPPs had not delivered the speed and efficiency the country needed, blaming transparency issues, inter-agency friction, institutional coordination problems and other bottlenecks.

“There are legal framework issues and institutional issues. In addressing these, this Bill is intended to resolve the statutory and legal constraints,” he said.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in his capacity as the Finance, Planning and Economic Development Minister.

title: Tea export earnings cross  $ 1 b mark by September | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:25
-     - 10

Customs data analysed by Siyaka Research indicates that Sri Lanka’s tea export earnings reached approximately $ 1.083 billion during the January–September 2026 period, compared with $ 1.163 billion earned during the corresponding period of the previous year.

 Despite September export volumes declining to 23 MnKg from 23.7 MnKg a year earlier, cumulative earnings in Sri Lankan Rupees increased to Rs. 350 billion from Rs. 347 billion. This improvement was largely attributable to the depreciation of the Rupee against the 

US dollar.

Total tea export volumes for the nine-month period amounted to 189.4 MnKg, down 4% from 198.3 MnKg recorded in 2025. The decline in export volumes was less pronounced than the depreciation of the rupee over the period, helping to support rupee-denominated export earnings despite lower USD earnings.

 Value-added tea exports continued to account for approximately 58% of total exports. Tea in packets, tea bags and instant tea remained the principal contributors to this segment, underscoring the continued importance of value addition to Sri Lanka’s tea export trade.

 

Against the backdrop of ongoing turmoil in the Middle East, export flows to and through Turkey recorded a significant increase of 134%, rising to 35.7 MnKg from 15.2 MnKg a year earlier.

Iraq, traditionally one of Sri Lanka’s key tea destinations, recorded a sharp decline in imports to 18.4 MnKg from 30 MnKg in the corresponding period of 2025. Russia maintained relatively steady volumes at 16.9 MnKg, while exports to Azerbaijan increased by 34% to 9 MnKg.

 

Shipments to China declined by 10% year-on-year to 7.1 MnKg. Libya also recorded a substantial reduction, with volumes falling from 15.9 MnKg to 6.6 MnKg, reflecting changes in shipment patterns and the movement of goods through alternative routes.

 

Exports to Syria improved by 5% to 6.4 MnKg, while shipments to Jordan increased by 51% to 6.3 MnKg, indicating a shift in trade flows amid the regional disruptions. Saudi Arabia continued to perform steadily, with Sri Lanka shipping 6.3 MnKg during the period, broadly in line with the previous year.

 

Chile rounded off the top ten destinations, with exports declining sharply to 6.3 MnKg from 8.5 MnKg a year earlier. Chile’s total tea imports reached a five-year high of 21.8 MnKg in 2025. However, the latest figures suggest that the market may be relinquishing some of those gains in 2026.

title: Cabinet nod for revised Rs. 15.08 b  plan to complete Kolonnawa Stormwater Drainage project | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:24
-     - 10

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a new plan to complete the remaining work on the Kolonnawa Stormwater Drainage and Environment Improvement Project at an estimated cost of Rs. 15,077.82 million, to be implemented over three years.

The construction on the project began in 2019, but the pre-planned implementation of its components was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and the 

economic recession that 

followed in Sri Lanka. 

A new project plan and cost estimate were therefore prepared for the remaining tasks.

As per the revised plan, work will include completing the construction of the Salalihini Mawatha canal, which is currently under construction, over a length of 3,250 metres, and building the 3,868-metre Dahamwala canal. Specialised works, such as creating water ponds and water retention areas, will also be carried out.

The plan also provides for the repair of the 4,475-metre Passiyana canal and the 650-metre Dandukotuwa canal, as well as the repair of the Dandutota flood gate. Three mobile pumps, each capable of pumping stormwater at a rate of one cubic metre per second, will also be installed.

In addition, a relief allowance proposal estimated at Rs. 1,015 million will be implemented to pay compensation. It takes into account the acquisition of essential land within the project area and the impact on the daily livelihoods of affected families.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake.

title: Access Engineering weighs fallout of terminated logistics hub JV | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:23
-     - 8

Access Engineering PLC expects to recover about Rs. 1.45 billion of the Rs. 1.76 billion it invested in the South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub, after the venture’s shareholders agreed not to proceed with the project, leaving the company to recognise a loss of about Rs. 310 million in its own financial statements.

The shareholders of South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub Ltd. mutually agreed to abandon the project in view of changes in external circumstances, including adjustments to its implementation environment and timetable, together with the respective commercial considerations of the parties, the company said. 

They have agreed to enter into a settlement agreement for the orderly termination of the project and related agreements.

Access Engineering holds a 15% stake in South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub. Under the settlement, it is expected to receive $ 3.29 million, about Rs. 1.09 billion, as its proportionate share of the settlement refund, together with about Rs. 365 million representing its share of the available distributable funds. Total recovery is estimated at about Rs. 1.45 billion, based on an indicative exchange rate of Rs. 331 to the dollar.

The impact differs between the Group and the company. In its audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 March, 2026, the Group had already recognised its share of the venture’s losses, amounting to about Rs. 387 million, reducing the investment’s carrying value, the value at which it is recorded in the accounts, to about Rs. 1.38 billion. As the anticipated settlement proceeds exceed that carrying value, no further material financial loss is presently anticipated in the Group’s consolidated accounts.

In the company’s own financial statements, however, the investment is carried at its original cost of Rs. 1.76 billion. Recovering about Rs. 1.45 billion would therefore result in a company-level loss of about Rs. 310 million.

The estimates are subject to exchange rates applicable on the actual transaction or payment dates, final settlement arrangements and applicable accounting adjustments, the company said.

The project was launched in April 2023 as a $ 392 million, 50-year Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) venture to build what was billed as South Asia’s largest commercial and logistics complex in the Port of Colombo, with China Merchants Port Holdings (CMPort) holding a 70% stake, and the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) and Access Engineering each holding 15%. The complex was to offer 530,000 cubic metres of storage capacity in an eight-floor building.

title: Resecurity (USA) named Strategic Partner for 12th Annual Cyber Security Summit 2026 in Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:22
-     - 9

Resecurity Senior Vice President Mark Kelly (right) exchanging the agreement with CICRA Holdings Group Executive Director/CEO Boshan Dayaratne in the presence of Director Amali Subasinghe

The 12th Annual Cyber Security Summit 2026 has announced that Resecurity (USA), a leading global provider of cybersecurity and intelligence solutions from Los Angeles (California), has joined as the official Strategic Partner. 

This landmark collaboration marks a significant milestone for the summit, bringing world-class US technology, expertise, and resources to the forefront of Sri Lanka’s premier cybersecurity event.

Resecurity is renowned for its next-generation cybersecurity solutions, providing unparalleled protection against sophisticated cyber threats.

Trusted by Fortune 500 companies, government agencies, and military organizations worldwide, Resecurity empowers clients with actionable intelligence and advanced technology to predict, prevent, and respond to cyber-attacks. Their presence as Strategic Partner underscores the summit’s commitment to bringing the highest calibre of global expertise to the region.

The 12th Annual Cyber Security Summit (https://cybersecuritysummit.lk), organised by CICRA and Daily FT, is Sri Lanka’s premier cybersecurity event. This year’s summit is entirely focused on the latest technological advance, Artificial Intelligence, and is dedicated to answering one critical question: “Is your organisation ready for AI-based cyberattacks?”

Scheduled on 18 and 19 November at the Cinnamon Grand, Colombo, the summit will bring together global experts, industry leaders, and policymakers to discuss the evolving threat landscape and provide actionable solutions for the audience.

Day one, 18 November, features the exclusive CEO Forum themed “Why Cyber Security Should Be a Boardroom Discussion.” With recent incidents in the country, the Companies Act, and the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) now holding board members personally liable for breaches, cybersecurity is no longer an IT issue, it is a governance imperative.

CICRA Holdings Group Executive Director/CEO Boshan Dayaratne said: “Whether we like it or not, most companies are already using AI in their day-to-day operations. CEOs and board members must be aware of whether those AI systems are being used responsibly and ethically, and must set a robust AI governance framework.” 

The CEO Forum is by invitation only. CEOs who have not received their invitation are welcome to contact the summit secretariat to request one.

As Strategic Partner, Resecurity will be deeply integrated into the summit’s three core events, ensuring attendees gain hands-on, world-class experience:

The CTF Challenge: The summit will host a thrilling Capture the Flag (CTF) competition using a world-renowned platform that is utilised in prestigious events globally, including the recent UN Summit in New York. This is an open invitation to all companies to form teams of four and enter the challenge. It is a unique opportunity to showcase your team’s capabilities, test your skills, and compete on a global stage against top talent. Event is scheduled on 14 November 2026, registrations are now open on https://cybersecuritysummit.lk

Expert Speaker Sessions: Resecurity will be sending globally recognised resources to speak at the summit on 18 and 19 November at the Cinnamon Grand. Their insights will provide attendees with a deep understanding of the current threat landscape and the future of cyber defence.

The “Night Hack” Showdown: Resecurity has agreed to headline the summit’s famous closing event, the “Night Hack.” They will present a thrilling live demonstration of AI hacking and defending, showcasing the real-world implications of the technologies discussed throughout the summit.

The central theme of this year’s summit is a critical question for every organisation. “AI is no longer a theoretical concept; it is a weaponised reality. The question we must ask ourselves is not if an AI-based attack will happen, but when. Are we ready? The 12th Annual Cyber Security Summit is designed to provide the answers. By partnering with a global powerhouse like Resecurity, we are not just asking the question, we are providing the platform, the knowledge, and the tools to build a resilient future,” added Dayaratne.

The agreement was formalized by Resecurity Senior Vice President Mark Kelly, who flew down to Sri Lanka to sign the partnership with the summit organizers.

Resecurity Head of Business Development (SAARC) Rajan Pant said: “Resecurity is proud to be the Strategic Partner of the 12th Annual Cyber Security Summit. We have great respect for CICRA’s vision and are committed to working with them to establish US technology and solutions in Sri Lanka.  This summit is the perfect launch-pad for this initiative, and we look forward to a successful and impactful collaboration between US and Sri Lankan Cybersecurity professionals.” 

The summit is expected to be a sell-out event. Registrations for the summit and the CTF challenge are now open. To secure your place and register your team of four for the CTF, please logon to https://cybersecuritysummit.lk

title: Premium International Injectable advances pharmaceutical manufacturing ambitions in Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:01
-     - 4

Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa inspects the advanced technical machinery and production processes during his tour of the Premium International Injectable Ltd., manufacturing facility, guided by the company’s management

Premium International Injectable Ltd., Managing Director and CEO Thushira Raddella in discussions with Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa and key stakeholders regarding the progress of the pharmaceutical project and future sector investments

An exterior view of the state-of-the-art pharmaceutical manufacturing facility developed by Premium International Injectable Ltd., to European standards within a Board of Investment (BOI) zone

Premium International Injectable Ltd., is advancing the development of its pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Sri Lanka, marking a significant step in the company’s commitment to strengthening local manufacturing capabilities and establishing a foundation for future growth in the country’s pharmaceutical sector.

The state-of-the-art facility, which is being developed to European standards within a Board of Investment (BOI) zone, is intended to support the manufacture of biotechnology-based insulin and generic Small Volume Parenteral (SVP) products. The plant is also geared to receive EU GMP certification, which is issued by National Competent Authorities (NCAs) within European Union member states. The project reflects the company’s ambition to establish a long-term manufacturing presence in Sri Lanka while exploring opportunities to expand its production capabilities in response to market requirements.

The visit by Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa provided an opportunity to review the facility’s development and highlight the company’s plans for pharmaceutical manufacturing in Sri Lanka. It also provided an opportunity to discuss the role of private-sector investment in developing local manufacturing capabilities and strengthening the country’s pharmaceutical industry.

Premium International Injectable Managing Director and CEO Thushira Raddella said: “Our investment in this facility reflects our long-term commitment to Sri Lanka and our confidence in the opportunities available within the country’s pharmaceutical manufacturing sector. We are focused on progressing the project towards completion and establishing a strong foundation for future growth. Beyond the current facility, we see opportunities to explore additional product strengths, doses and formulations in response to market requirements, while building strategic relationships that can support the next phase of our development.”

The facility’s planned focus on biotechnology-based insulin and generic SVP products represents an opportunity to develop specialised pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities locally. Insulin manufacturing involves specific biotechnology and production requirements, while SVP products encompass injectable medicines administered in relatively small volumes. Both areas require appropriate manufacturing infrastructure, robust quality systems and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The development of local pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities has the potential to contribute to the resilience of medicine supply chains, broaden the country’s industrial capabilities and create opportunities for skills development and collaboration across the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors.

Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said: “Developing pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities in Sri Lanka presents an opportunity to strengthen medicine supply resilience and support the country’s healthcare sector. Such initiatives must be underpinned by robust quality standards, regulatory compliance and collaboration between the public and private sectors.”

Premium International Injectable is also engaging with relevant institutional and industry stakeholders, including the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation (SPMC), where applicable, as it advances its manufacturing plans. Such engagement provides an opportunity to explore areas of mutual interest and understand the requirements and opportunities within Sri Lanka’s pharmaceutical manufacturing landscape.

The company’s longer-term vision extends beyond the current facility. Subject to market demand, technical feasibility and the relevant regulatory requirements, it intends to explore opportunities to introduce additional product strengths, doses and formulations. This approach would allow the company to assess future manufacturing opportunities in line with evolving healthcare needs and the commercial requirements of the local market.

As the project progresses towards completion, Premium International Injectable is also open to discussions with potential investors, strategic partners, suppliers and other businesses interested in contributing to the development of pharmaceutical manufacturing in Sri Lanka. These opportunities could support future expansion, strengthen business relationships and create a broader platform for collaboration within the sector.

title: Cabinet approves extension of Suraksha Student Insurance Scheme with expanded benefits | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:00
-     - 4

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved revising the existing agreement between the Education Ministry and Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation for continued implementation of the Suraksha Student Insurance Program for the period from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027, with several new benefits added.

The program aims to create the environment necessary for students facing obstacles due to health issues to overcome barriers and continue their education without interruption. Students in Government schools, Government-approved private schools, Pirivenas and assisted special schools are eligible.

Announcing the decision, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa under the revised agreement, students will be able to claim up to Rs. 75,000 for the repair of hearing accessories and related service charges. Those on long-term medication for conditions such as chronic kidney disease and chronic inflammatory arthritis can claim up to Rs. 20,000.

“A further Rs. 20,000 can be claimed for the cost of tests, including malignancy screening for skin cancer, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), osteoporosis screening, and screening for Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C and HIV,” he said at the weekly post-Cabinet meeting media briefing yesterday.

Dr. Jayatissa said under the critical illness category, "Cancer Treatment" has been revised to "Cancer Treatment and related Testing," with cover extended to PET scans and to major surgeries for hip, shoulder and knee joint replacements required due to sudden accidents.

In addition, a payment of Rs. 100,000 will be made under the accidental category for student deaths caused by sudden accidents during activities organised by institutions under the Education Ministry and conducted under the supervision of educational authorities, such as educational tours, excursions and sports meets, whether within or outside the school.

Pointing out that the extended benefits will greatly help the students, he noted that although the Government allocated Rs. 2,290 million in 2024/25 year only Rs. 1,510 million was utilised, while for the year 2025/26 the allocation was Rs. 2,351 million and only Rs. 1,501 million was used.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya, in her capacity as Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Minister.
